Category of Enforcement: Securities Fraud / Wire Fraud / Money Laundering
Description of Violation: Jury convicted the former CEO of decentralised token SafeMoon (peak market cap ~$8 billion) of conspiracy to commit securities fraud, wire fraud and money laundering for diverting liquidity-pool funds for personal use.
Additional Notes: A genuine fraud conviction secured despite the broader 2025 enforcement slowdown, illustrating the DOJ's narrowed-but-real fraud focus.

Description of Violation: Charged Unicoin and three senior executives, including its general counsel, with fraud for selling rights certificates purportedly redeemable for crypto assets while making false claims about underlying collateral.
Amount of Fine: $37,500 (general counsel personal penalty); company resolution ongoing
Outcome: Charges Filed; partial settlement with individual defendant
Relevant Regulations Violated: Securities Act of 1933, Securities Exchange Act of 1934
Additional Notes: Shows the new SEC will still bring affirmative fraud cases even while dismantling registration-only litigation.

Description of Violation: SEC voluntarily dismissed its remaining 2023 civil securities suit against Binance and former CEO Changpeng Zhao; the parallel 2023 DOJ/CFTC/FinCEN/OFAC criminal and AML resolutions (totalling $4.3bn) remain in force and are unaffected.
Amount of Fine: $0 (SEC civil claims dismissed); prior $4.3bn DOJ/CFTC/Treasury settlement stands
Outcome: Dismissed with Prejudice (SEC civil action only)
Additional Notes: Illustrates the dataset's key analytical nuance: criminal/AML penalties from the Biden era were not unwound, only the SEC's civil registration theory.

Description of Violation: SEC voluntarily dismissed its separate 20-Nov-2023 lawsuit against crypto exchange Kraken alleging it operated as an unregistered securities exchange, broker, dealer and clearing agency (distinct from Kraken's earlier, already-settled Feb-2023 staking-program case).
Additional Notes: Completed the rollback of the SEC's 'big four' exchange suits (Coinbase, Binance, Kraken, plus closed Gemini investigation). Cross-reference: see the staking-program settlement at Case ID 3:23-cv-00588 for Kraken's separate, earlier, already-resolved matter.

Description of Violation: Russian national indicted for using his company Evita to enable sanctioned Russian banks and entities to obtain U.S. dollars and stablecoins via crypto, laundering funds and operating an unlicensed money-transmitting business.
Relevant Regulations Violated: IEEPA, Bank Secrecy Act, Wire Fraud Statutes
Additional Notes: Demonstrates DOJ's continued 'fraud and sanctions-evasion' carve-out under the Blanche Memo even amid broad deprioritisation of registration cases.

Description of Violation: DOJ, supported by blockchain-analytics tooling, disrupted a terrorist-financing scheme that used crypto wallets to raise and transfer approximately $200,000 for Hamas-linked operatives, resulting in seizure of the funds.
Relevant Regulations Violated: IEEPA, Anti-Terrorism Act, Bank Secrecy Act
Additional Notes: Textbook example of the 'carve-out' the Blanche Memo explicitly preserved: crypto-enabled terrorism financing remains a top DOJ priority despite the registration-enforcement retreat.

Description of Violation: SEC staff issued a statement clarifying that most 'memecoins' lack the characteristics of securities under the Howey test and therefore fall outside SEC registration requirements.
Additional Notes: Removes an entire token category from the registration-enforcement pipeline, directly shrinking the future caseload.

Description of Violation: President Trump signed the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act into law, creating the first comprehensive federal regulatory framework for payment stablecoins, mandating 1:1 reserve backing in cash and short-term Treasurys, monthly reserve disclosures, and BSA/AML obligations for issuers.
Relevant Regulations Violated: GENIUS Act of 2025; amends Bank Secrecy Act, Securities Act, Commodity Exchange Act
Additional Notes: Central legislative event motivating Section 3 of this assessment; reclassifies compliant payment stablecoins as neither securities nor commodities, divesting SEC/CFTC jurisdiction over them.

Description of Violation: CFTC's first action against a digital-asset intermediary, alleging Falcon Labs connected U.S. customers to unregistered and unlawfully operating offshore trading platforms.
Additional Notes: Director of Enforcement Ian McGinley cited this as evidence the CFTC still pursues 'gatekeepers' that route US persons to unlawful platforms, even amid the broader slowdown.

Entity/Individual: Systematic Alpha Management LLC / Peter Kambolin
Description of Violation: CFTC obtained a $2.8 million consent judgment against a commodity trading adviser and its principal for fraudulently allocating profitable crypto and FX futures trades to proprietary accounts while assigning losses to customer pools.
Additional Notes: Parallel criminal case (Kambolin pleaded guilty Oct-2023) was the first cherry-picking prosecution involving digital-asset futures; demonstrates continuity of CFTC fraud enforcement post-reset.

Entity/Individual: Three Unregistered Crypto Trading Platforms and Four Investment Clubs
Description of Violation: Charged a network of purported crypto trading platforms and affiliated investment clubs with running a coordinated scheme that solicited retail investors via social media with false promises of guaranteed returns.
Relevant Regulations Violated: Securities Act of 1933, Securities Exchange Act of 1934
Additional Notes: Representative of the SEC's post-reset enforcement mix: social-media retail fraud remains a priority even as registration theory cases are abandoned.

Description of Violation: SEC voluntarily dismissed its high-profile cybersecurity disclosure fraud action against SolarWinds and its CISO arising from the 2020 SUNBURST nation-state intrusion, following a related 2024 partial dismissal by the district court.
Additional Notes: Not a crypto case itself, but evidences the same Atkins-era 'back to basics' retreat pattern from novel-theory enforcement that characterises the 2025 crypto dismissals; included for the dataset's enforcement-trend control group.

Description of Violation: CFTC amended its Rules of Practice and investigation procedures to require comprehensive, evidence-cited memoranda before staff can recommend settlements, and reformed the Wells-notice process to increase transparency for respondents.
Additional Notes: Procedural tightening that, combined with halved enforcement staffing, structurally reduces the agency's capacity to bring rapid registration-style crypto cases going forward.

Entity/Individual: Pinnacle Advisors, LLC and Individual Respondents
Description of Violation: SEC dismissed its civil enforcement action against an investment advisory firm and four individuals over alleged undisclosed conflicts in crypto-fund fee arrangements, citing reassessment of litigation priorities.
Additional Notes: Further evidence the dismissal pattern extended beyond the largest exchanges to mid-size adviser-level crypto-adjacent cases.

Description of Violation: SEC filed proposed final consent judgments against former FTX engineer Gary Wang and former Alameda Research CEO Caroline Ellison, formalising injunctions and disgorgement tied to their cooperation in the FTX fraud prosecution.
Amount of Fine: Disgorgement and penalties per individual cooperation agreements (amounts under seal)
Additional Notes: Confirms that core FTX-related fraud accountability proceeded to conclusion even as the broader crypto enforcement program contracted sharply.

Description of Violation: OFAC designated operators of a successor exchange to the previously sanctioned Garantex platform for facilitating ransomware and darknet-market related cryptocurrency transactions in violation of sanctions.
Additional Notes: OFAC sanctions activity remained largely insulated from the SEC/CFTC/DOJ civil-enforcement pullback, reflecting its distinct national-security mandate.

Entity/Individual: Morocoin Tech Corp.; Berge Blockchain Technology Co.; Cirkor Inc.; AI Wealth Inc.; Lane Wealth Inc.; AI Investment Education Foundation; Zenith Asset Tech Foundation
Description of Violation: Charged a network of seven entities for operating fraudulent 'investment clubs' via WhatsApp and social media that lured investors using AI-generated investment tips into funding accounts on fabricated crypto trading platforms purporting to hold government licences, then offered fake 'Security Token Offerings' from non-existent issuing companies; investors who tried to withdraw funds were defrauded further.
Amount of Fine: N/A (disgorgement and penalties sought; litigation ongoing)
Relevant Regulations Violated: Securities Act of 1933, Securities Exchange Act of 1934
Additional Notes: Illustrates the SEC's continuing, indeed expanding, affirmative-fraud caseload even as registration-theory litigation against legitimate exchanges was being dismissed throughout 2025; scheme ran from January 2024 to January 2025, spanning both administrations.

Entity/Individual: Department of Justice (National Fraud Enforcement Division)
Description of Violation: DOJ announced creation of a new National Fraud Enforcement Division consolidating fraud-focused units, signalling a pivot of resources toward general fraud (including crypto-enabled fraud) rather than crypto-specific regulatory enforcement.
Additional Notes: Consistent with the Blanche Memo's framing: crypto fraud is folded into general fraud enforcement rather than treated as a freestanding crypto-enforcement priority.

Entity/Individual: SEC Division of Enforcement (FY2025 Annual Report)
Description of Violation: SEC published its FY2025 enforcement statistics: 313 new actions (lowest in a decade, down 27% from FY2024) and $808 million in monetary settlements (down 45% YoY); the report characterised the prior administration's high-volume crypto enforcement as 'misallocated resources.'
Additional Notes: Key quantitative anchor for the regulatory-easing analysis required by the CA1 brief; figures used directly in the EDA narrative.

Entity/Individual: Foreign Binary Options Fraud Network (5 Entities, 3 Individuals)
Description of Violation: CFTC obtained a default judgment against five foreign entities and three foreign individuals for operating an illegal off-exchange binary-options scheme that manipulated trading platform settings and blocked customer withdrawals.
Additional Notes: Largest single recovery in the post-2025-reset period; shows the CFTC's 'back-to-basics' fraud docket can still produce nine-figure judgments against bad-faith foreign actors.

Description of Violation: SEC Chairman Paul Atkins announced staff guidance permitting SEC registrants to use GENIUS Act-compliant payment stablecoins for trade settlement and margining, formally bridging traditional securities infrastructure with the new stablecoin regime.
Relevant Regulations Violated: GENIUS Act of 2025; Securities Exchange Act of 1934
Additional Notes: Most recent regulatory development in the dataset; illustrates the shift from enforcement-driven to integration-driven crypto policy that frames the Section 1 and Section 3 discussion.
